title: Jabesh-gilead
lead: A town east of the Jordan in Gilead, bound to Saul's house by rescue and loyalty. Its people were nearly wiped out in the war on Benjamin, rescued by Saul at the start of his reign, and risked their lives to bury him.

sections.b: Jabesh-gilead first appears when it sends no men to the war against Benjamin, and its young women are taken as wives for the surviving Benjaminites (Judges 21:8–14), a tie that may explain its later bond with Saul of Benjamin. Saul's first act as king is to rescue the town from Nahash the Ammonite (1 Samuel 11:1–11). At the end, its men march through the night to take the bodies of Saul and his sons from the wall of Beth-shan and bury them (1 Samuel 31:11–13). David praises their loyal love (2 Samuel 2:4–7) and later moves the bones to Benjamin (2 Samuel 21:12–14).
